attributes.readMe:
# Talent & Resource Tracker

## Summary
An applicant tracking system (ATS) and employee resource manager. Tabs: Dashboard (headcount, open pipeline, average time-to-hire), Directory (query-driven employee card list), Pipeline (candidates by stage with Approve/Reject actions), Calendar (interview scheduling month grid), and Org Chart (manager-hierarchy tree).

## Import
```ts
import { TalentResourceTracker } from './talent-resource-tracker';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As the app shell.** One CardDef with nine `linksToMany` collections and
eight tabs. `prefersWideFormat = true`; it defines only `isolated`, because it
is opened as a workspace rather than embedded.

**2. As a work queue.** The Pipeline tab is a kanban whose columns are the
Candidate stages. Dropping a card runs the matching command —
`AdvanceToOfferCommand` into offer, `ApproveOfferCommand` into hired,
`RejectCandidateCommand` into rejected — so a drag and a button click produce
the same result.

**3. As a live directory.** The Directory tab is the **only** tab that queries
the realm (`CardList` filtered by type + name + department). The other seven
read the card's own `linksToMany` arrays, which is why a newly created Meeting
or Employee must be linked to the tracker to appear on the Calendar or Org
Chart — and why the Directory is immune to that.

**4. As a dashboard.** Stat tiles plus a stage-distribution donut computed from
the linked candidates; `avgTimeToHire` averages `timeToHire` across hires.

**5. As an org chart.** `buildOrgTree` folds the linked Employees' `manager`
edges into a forest, promoting orphans to roots rather than dropping them.

## Template Usage
The isolated view is the whole app. Approve/Reject buttons on the Pipeline tab run the ApproveOfferCommand / RejectCandidateCommand against the selected candidate.

**Non-goals:** catalog packaging (deliberately deferred project-wide); multi-org tenancy.
